title: Pre-Discovery Observational Predictions of Chronodynamic Relativity for 2026-2028 Astronomical Surveys and Laboratory Experiments
description: Establishes a formal, citable pre-discovery baseline for Chronodynamic Relativity across nine major experimental domains ahead of forthcoming data releases between late 2026 and 2028. Evaluates exact parameter-free prediction bounds for: (1) Gaia DR4 wide binary asymptotic velocity floor (v_flat = 0.425 km/s for 1.5 M_sun beyond 5.79 kAU); (2) JWST cosmic dawn true expansion redshift mapping (z_obs = 14.32 to z_exp = 10.45, expanding available cosmic time by +52%); (3) DESI Year 5 apparent evolving dark energy (w_0 = -0.852, w_a = -0.395); (4) Euclid DR1 suppressed cosmic shear clustering (S_8 = 0.763); (5) Simons Observatory primordial tensor mode ceiling (r < 0.005); (6) Rubin LSST distance duality break (eta(z=1) = 0.9205); (7) Quasar non-kinematic dipole (906 km/s); (8) Bose-Marletto-Vedral (BMV) witness protocol observing suppression of gravitationally induced entanglement (W <= 1) and classical dephasing floor; and (9) Fine-structure drift. Establishes six explicit empirical falsification criteria.
notes: Version 1.0.0 Initial Pre-Discovery Baseline: Locked mathematical predictions across nine empirical domains prior to Gaia DR4 (Dec 2, 2026), DESI Year 5, Euclid DR1, and JWST Cycles 5/6.
